title: Active Inference Agent Simulations: Adaptive Advantages of Somatic Markers
description: Seven-architecture active-inference simulation benchmark with separate held-out human IGT model comparison; CP-3a calibration and identifiability are prerequisites. Pred 2.F–2.G are exploratory.

primary_hypothesis: Calibrated APGI converges in the 50–80-trial human benchmark, exhibits registered interoceptive dominance and somatic temporal precedence, shows lesion specificity, and improves held-out human-data fit over Standard PP and GNWT-only.

apgi_parameters.model: Reduced empirical specification: seven core quantities plus somatic modulation; not eight freely fitted parameters in every dataset.

gamma_sig.role: population-fixed model sigmoid steepness; distinct from alpha_psy

beta_SM.role: somatic modulation gain; not independently identifiable from Pi_i using behavior alone

kappa.role: energy-information bridge only; never ignition steepness

apgi_parameters.gain_interpretation: Pi_i in the reduced confirmatory model is salience-weighted gain; HEP is a candidate indicator, not a direct inverse-variance measurement.
apgi_parameters.accumulation: S_next=(1-a_S)*S+a_S*u; a_S=1-exp(-dt/tau_S); u uses calibration-fixed relative gains and excess magnitudes abs(z)-sqrt(2/pi).
apgi_parameters.ignition: p_k=1-exp(-r_max*sigmoid(gamma_sig*(S-theta))*dt); single trial-window sigmoid sampling is a distinct convention, never interchanged within a protocol.
apgi_parameters.time_step: dt=0.01 s reduced reference; dt<=min(tau_S,tau_theta,tau_Pi)/10; active reservoir additionally requires dt<=tau_res/10.
apgi_parameters.parameter_manifest_status: Required before confirmatory fitting; no unspecified coefficient is assigned a legacy default.

quality_and_decision_rules.data_admissibility: Apply registered quality gates before inference. Inadmissible data are exploratory, receive no Scenario A–F, and carry no framework vote.

scenarios.A: Scenario A — Confirmed. p < α and BF₁₀ ≥ 100. Both streams converge on H₁. Counted toward framework-level BY-FDR confirmation and toward the joint Bayesian meta-analysis. No additional replication is required before the claim is filed.
scenarios.B: Scenario B — Tentative confirmation. p < α and 3 ≤ BF₁₀ < 100. The frequentist threshold is met but Bayesian evidence is moderate rather than strong; reported as "frequentist-significant, Bayesian moderate." One pre-registered independent replication is required before the result is elevated to confirmatory status, and that replication is registered before the primary result is published.
scenarios.C: Scenario C — Discordant (frequentist-positive, Bayesian-null). p < α and BF₁₀ < 3. The frequentist threshold is met but the Bayes factor provides less than moderate evidence for H₁ and may favor H₀. Classified as equivocal: the result neither confirms nor falsifies the prediction. It is flagged as equivocal in the results and recorded in the analysis log (not in the protocol-deviation register, which is reserved for departures from registered procedure). Independent replication at ≥ 90% power is required before any interpretation is made.
scenarios.D: Scenario D — Bayesian positive (without frequentist significance). p ≥ α and BF₁₀ ≥ 100. Strong probabilistic support for H₁ while the NHST threshold is missed. Not counted toward BY-FDR (which operates on the frequentist p-values). The original study plus one pre-registered replication are required for elevation to confirmatory status.
scenarios.E: Scenario E — Bayesian falsification. p ≥ α and BF₀₁ ≥ 6. The frequentist result is nonsignificant and the Bayesian analysis supports H₀. Classified as provisional falsification of the specific sub-prediction and reported as such in the primary manuscript. A single Scenario E result triggers independent replication at ≥ 90% power before the sub-prediction is declared definitively falsified, and triggers review of whether the framework-level falsification threshold has been reached (two or more Scenario E results across primary protocols; framework-level decision rule).
scenarios.F: Scenario F — Indeterminate. p ≥ α and 1/6 < BF₁₀ < 100 (i.e., neither BF₁₀ ≥ 100 nor BF₀₁ ≥ 6). Neither stream reaches a decision threshold. Classified as inconclusive: it carries no confirmatory or falsifying weight and is reported transparently as indeterminate. It may motivate a pre-registered replication but does not by itself trigger one, and it is never counted toward BY-FDR confirmation or framework-level falsification.

quality_and_decision_rules.framework_confirmation: At least 4/5 primary protocols, combined hierarchical BF10>=100, and at most one Scenario E protocol. Protocol 0 is a gate; 2 contributes F2; 6 is CE.
quality_and_decision_rules.protocol_alpha_specification: Protocol 2 (Somatic-AgentSim): Permutation Go/No-Go tests α = 0.01, two-tailed, 10,000 permutations. Model comparison is adjudicated on ΔBIC, not Bayes factors: Pred 2.E requires ΔBIC ≥ 10 in favor of APGI-full against each of Standard PP and GNWT-only, with cross-validation log-likelihood improvement p < 0.01. Framework-falsifier F2 is triggered at ΔBIC ≤ 0 versus the best alternative across all pre-registered Protocol 2 datasets. The BF₁₀ ≥ 100 entry in Table 3 (§3.1.2) is a target for the hierarchical Bayesian human-IGT fit and is not the Pred 2.E or F2 decision criterion.
quality_and_decision_rules.decision_precedence: Prediction-specific estimands, interval/evidence rules and admissibility gates govern over abbreviated source summaries. The A–F matrix applies only where both frequentist and Bayesian hypotheses are explicitly defined; do not invent a point-null Bayes factor. Nonsignificance or a point estimate alone does not establish equivalence or falsification; specificity requires a direct contrast. Unresolved interval bounds or multiplicity allocations require prospective analysis lock.

specification_sections.heading: Somatic Marker Adaptive Advantage and Ignition-Enabled Flexibility
specification_sections.text: Protocol 2 (Somatic-AgentSim) tests whether somatic markers (M) and precision-weighted ignition confer genuine adaptive advantages over architectures that lack them. The benchmark is convergence speed on the Iowa Gambling Task (IGT; Bechara et al., 1997): a human-calibrated standard that competing computational architectures — pure predictive processing and GNWT-only agents — must be measured against on equal footing.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Agent Architecture
specification_sections.text: The computational protocol implements a hierarchical active inference agent with: separate interoceptive and exteroceptive generative models (both 3-level hierarchies); dynamic precision-weighting (Πᵉ and Πⁱ updated online); somatic marker learning where M(c,a) updates via reward prediction errors; a global workspace layer governed by the ignition equation (Sₜ > θₜ); and threshold adaptation following the Euler discretization of the canonical threshold equation (§1.5): θₜ₊₁ = θₜ + Δt·[−(θₜ − θ₀)/τ_θ + c_θ·Cₜ − Δ_info·V_info,t + γ_NE·NE(t)].
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Comparison Architectures
specification_sections.text:
Standard PP (Pure Predictive Processing): no global ignition layer; continuous processing. Expected convergence: 150+ trials.

GNWT-only: ignition without somatic markers or precision-weighting. Expected convergence: 100–120 trials.

APGI-full: full architecture as specified. Predicted convergence: 50–80 trials.

β_SM agent: Full APGI architecture with somatic gain pathway disabled (β_SM = 0). Tests pathway specificity of the somatic marker channel (Pred 2.D).

Πⁱ-constant agent: Interoceptive precision held at baseline throughout (Πⁱ = constant). Tests adaptive value of precision updating.

α_M agent: metabolic-cost weighting disabled (α_M ≡ c_θ = 0, removing the cost term from dθ/dt). Tests dissociability of metabolic vs. interoceptive contributions.

Random-baseline agent: uniformly random action selection, providing the chance-performance floor and completing the five-agent lesion set (full APGI, β_SM-lesion, Πⁱ-lesion, α_M-lesion, random baseline) specified in the Protocols master; Standard PP and GNWT-only serve as BIC/convergence reference architectures, not lesion agents.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: M̂ Calibration Sub-Protocol CP-3a (required before confirmatory simulation)
specification_sections.text: The theoretical somatic marker weights γ_V = 0.6 and γ_A^SM = 0.3 in M̂(c,a) = γ_V·V(c,a) + γ_A^SM·A(c,a) must be empirically calibrated before Protocol 2 (Somatic-AgentSim) confirmatory analysis proceeds. Note: γ_A^SM (somatic-marker arousal weight, used only inside M̂(c,a)) is a distinct parameter from any general allostatic coupling weight elsewhere in the framework and must not be conflated with it; all references to this parameter in this document use the γ_A^SM notation, never bare γ_A.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Procedure
specification_sections.text: (1) Fit M̂(c,a) to human Iowa Gambling Task data from at least one published dataset (minimum N = 60; recommended: the open 'many labs' IGT dataset, N = 617; Steingroever et al., 2015). The in-vivo N = 80 sample (Table 3) is reserved for Pred 2.E and is not used for CP-3a, so calibration and test data never overlap. (2) Estimate γ_V and γ_A^SM via maximum likelihood. (3) If the 95% CI for γ_V lies entirely more than 0.15 from 0.6, or that for γ_A^SM entirely more than 0.15 from 0.3, recalibrate and amend the OSF pre-registration before confirmatory analysis. Calibrated γ values replace theoretical defaults in all reported analyses.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Task Environments
specification_sections.text:
Three task environments are simulated: (1) an Iowa Gambling Task variant with four decks carrying physiological penalties through simulated interoceptive costs; (2) volatile foraging in which reward statistics shift unpredictably and homeostatic costs vary by location; (3) threat–reward trade-offs in which high-reward options produce aversive interoceptive consequences.

Fixed task parameters (binding). Each environment comprises five experimental blocks of 100 trials (500 trials total), with the environmental volatility schedule σ_env = [0.1, 0.3, 0.6, 0.3, 0.1] across blocks 1–5. Pred 2.D's high-volatility contrast is evaluated on block 3 (σ_env = 0.6) against blocks 1 and 5 (σ_env = 0.1).

Seeds. N = 1,000 independent seeds per condition (minimum admissible N = 500) supply the bootstrapped confidence intervals. Seeds are assigned deterministically as seed = condition_index × 1000 + replicate_index (NumPy default_rng), replicate_index 0–999 per condition, so that every run is independently reproducible from the released code. This per-condition scheme supersedes the single-integer entry P2 = 20202 in the Analysis Manifest, which applies only to Protocol 2's human-IGT model-fitting MCMC, not to the simulation sweep.

Identifiability. The somatic-marker model operates via Πⁱ_eff = Πⁱ_baseline · exp(β_SM · M̂(c,a)), where M̂ integrates anticipated value V(c,a) and anticipated arousal A(c,a). In simulation, where M̂(c,a) is known, identifiability of β_SM and Πⁱ is checked with the Fisher Information Matrix (condition number < 100; dimensionless normalized cross-information R_ij = I_ij/√(I_ii I_jj), with max |R_ij| < 0.1 for the named parameter block and condition number < 100 on the same scaled matrix. This is distinct from covariance correlation computed from I⁻¹. The locked implementation states the parameter scaling, evaluation grid and chosen diagnostic; a local FIM check does not prove global structural identifiability. This does not contradict Table 1: in human behavioral data M̂ is latent, and the two parameters remain non-identifiable without the Protocol 0/5 manipulations. Failure of this pre-check halts confirmatory simulation and triggers a pre-registered amendment.

Environment. Python 3.11 (NumPy 1.26, SciPy 1.13).

specification_sections.heading: Computational Reproducibility
specification_sections.text: All simulations will use fixed random seeds; parameter sweeps will be logged; code will be containerized with Docker for exact environment replication. Simulations run in the pinned container (Python 3.11, NumPy 1.26, SciPy 1.13) on macOS, Windows or Linux hosts; requirements.txt and environment.yml committed to GitHub.

specification_sections.heading: Pred 2.A — Human-matching convergence benchmark
specification_sections.text: APGI agents learn to avoid long-term negative somatic outcomes within 50–80 trials, matching human Iowa Gambling Task performance (Bechara et al., 1997). This benchmark is the minimum criterion for claiming Functional Isomorphism. Convergence outside the 50–80 trial window — even with superior cumulative reward — does not satisfy Pred 2.A, because temporal matching to human performance is the operationalized claim, not reward maximization. Pure PP agents require 150+ trials; GNWT-only agents require 100–120 trials. Cumulative reward over 200 trials shows expected APGI advantage of 15–25% over GNWT-only, which in turn outperforms Pure PP. A reward ratio merely exceeding 1.15 at permutation p < 0.05 is insufficient without the temporal constraint — APGI must reach criterion within the human performance window.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 2.B — Interoceptive trigger composition (mechanistic, not consequential)
specification_sections.text:
Ignition events (Sₜ > θₜ) are triggered specifically when Πⁱ·|zⁱ| crosses the threshold. 70–85% of all ignition events must satisfy the interoceptive dominance criterion Πⁱ·|zⁱ| > Πᵉ·|zᵉ| because homeostatic threats prioritize ignition. This tests the triggering condition (somatic gating) rather than merely the downstream consequence (post-ignition action entropy) — the latter supports the computational advantage claim but does not validate the core somatic suppression mechanism that defines APGI's uniqueness.

Because the dominance proportion depends on the simulated environment's interoceptive-cost schedule, all environment parameters are fixed in the released configuration before any simulation is run, and Pred 2.B is interpreted as a property of the implemented model under those parameters, not as independent empirical evidence.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 2.C — Somatic-marker retrieval leads threshold crossing
specification_sections.text: Somatic-marker retrieval M̂ temporally precedes threshold crossing θₜ: the cross-correlation between M̂ activation and the ignition signal Bₜ peaks at negative lag, with M̂ leading by ≥ 1 trial in ≥ 75% of ignition events (Kendall τ > 0.3 with n = 1,000 seeds; τ = 0.3 is well above the detection floor at this n). Falsified if M̂ activation is simultaneous with or lags threshold crossing (cross-correlation peak at lag 0 or positive).
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 2.D — β_SM specificity
specification_sections.text: The β_SM lesion degrades performance more than any other single-parameter lesion (Πⁱ, α_M), with the deficit largest in high-volatility blocks (σ_env = 0.6). Confirming: β_SM-agent reward significantly lower than Πⁱ- and α_M-lesion agents under matched volatility (permutation p < 0.01, 10,000 permutations). Falsified if β_SM produces an equivalent or lesser deficit than Πⁱ under all volatility conditions.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 2.E — Model parsimony on human data
specification_sections.text: APGI-full achieves ΔBIC ≥ 10 versus both Standard PP and GNWT-only when fit to human IGT trial-by-trial choice sequences, with cross-validated log-likelihood improvement p < 0.01. Falsified if APGI BIC ≥ any alternative's BIC on any pre-registered dataset.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 2.F — Ignition enables deliberate strategy change
specification_sections.text: Exploratory (not part of the confirmatory Pred 2.A–2.E set). Post-ignition action-selection entropy increases relative to the pre-ignition baseline, and adaptive behavioral shifts correlate with ignition events beyond prediction-error magnitude alone. In the logistic regression P(strategy_change) ~ ignition + |ε| + controls, the ignition coefficient remains significant (p < 0.01) even when controlling for |ε|, indexing the behavioral-flexibility readout of ignition. This supports the computational-advantage claim but does not validate the core somatic triggering mechanism (Pred 2.B), and is therefore reported as exploratory.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Pred 2.G — Computational critical-slowing proxy (exploratory)
specification_sections.text: Exploratory (not part of the confirmatory Pred 2.A–2.E set). If clinical iEEG is unavailable, Protocol 2 supplies a computational proxy for the critical-slowing signature of Pred 6.C (PREREQUISITE, §2.1). Signal: the simulated ignition margin Δ(t) = S(t) − θ(t) of the full APGI agent in the three task environments, under the fixed task parameters and per-condition seeds above (N = 1,000 seeds per condition). Estimator: lag-1 autocorrelation (AC1) of Δ(t) in five consecutive non-overlapping 100-ms windows (10 steps each at Δt = 10 ms) spanning the 500 ms before each threshold crossing, and in matched windows before non-crossing epochs; no window spans a crossing or a post-ignition reset. Comparison: within each seed, Kendall τ between AC1 and window position, for crossing versus non-crossing epochs; the across-seed median τ is reported with a seed-level bootstrap 95% CI. Reporting rule: descriptive only. No confirmatory threshold applies, the Protocol 6 criterion (τ ≥ 0.40) is not imported, and no Pred 2.G result confirms, falsifies or substitutes for Pred 6.C.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Exploratory analysis — Volatility adaptation advantage (not a registered prediction)
specification_sections.text: Exploratory (not part of the confirmatory Pred 2.A–2.E set). APGI agents adapt 20–30% faster than GNWT-only agents in volatile foraging environments with shifting homeostatic costs, measured as trials to criterion after contingency shifts. This was a confirmatory prediction in prior drafts and is demoted here because it is not separable from Pred 2.A's convergence-speed criterion; it is reported alongside Pred 2.A and carries no framework-level weight.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: Model Comparison
specification_sections.text: Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) for model fit to human data; cross-validation on held-out trials; sensitivity analysis across parameter ranges (η, β_SM, θ₀). The reported 10,000-trial pilot-convergence result remains unverified until its configuration, seeds, code revision, convergence criterion and results are archived. Record whether pilot inspection informed these predictions; such pilot data are excluded from confirmatory evaluation. Without that archive, stable convergence is a working assumption rather than an established simulation finding.
specification_sections.role: source_context; curated structured decisions govern conflicts

specification_sections.heading: BIC application
specification_sections.text: BIC in Protocol 2 (Somatic-AgentSim) is computed in two distinct modes that must not be conflated: (1) Fit to human IGT data — all three agent architectures (APGI-full, GNWT-only, Standard PP) are fit to human participant trial-by-trial choice sequences using maximum likelihood estimation; BIC penalizes free parameter count and the architecture with the lowest group-level BIC is preferred. This is the primary model comparison (Pred 2.E). (2) Simulation benchmark — agents are run in forward-simulation mode on the task environment with fixed parameters to generate convergence and adaptation-speed curves (Pred 2.A and the exploratory volatility-adaptation analysis) and lesion comparisons (Pred 2.D); no BIC is computed here. These two analyses are complementary but distinct: superior simulation performance (Pred 2.A) demonstrates computational sufficiency; superior BIC fit to human data (Pred 2.E) demonstrates that APGI's additional parameters are warranted by the empirical signal. Both are required; neither alone constitutes validation.

methods_source_sections.heading: Outliers and influence
methods_source_sections.text:
4.3.2 Outlier and influential-observation policy

All rules below are fixed pre-collection and apply to every protocol unless a protocol body specifies otherwise; no post-hoc outlier rule may be introduced. (a) Trial level. Scalp-EEG trials exceeding the 150 µV peak-to-peak criterion (§4.2.1) are rejected; iEEG trials follow the interictal-discharge and |z| > 6 rule of §Protocol 6; behavioral trials in speeded detection tasks with RT < 150 ms or > 3 s are rejected as anticipations or lapses (Protocol 2 IGT and Protocol 7 bedside tasks use the rules in their protocol bodies). No further trial-level trimming is permitted. (b) Participant level. A participant is excluded only for a pre-registered admissibility failure (> 30% trial rejection, Data-Admissibility Gate; failed manipulation check; protocol violation). Statistical outlyingness is never itself an exclusion ground. (c) Observation level in models. Continuous predictors and outcomes are winsorized at ±3 SD within participant before entry into any confirmatory model; the untrimmed analysis is reported alongside as a mandatory sensitivity analysis, and a discrepancy in the confirmatory decision between the two is reported as an instability flag. (d) Influence. For every confirmatory regression or mixed model, Cook's distance is computed and observations with D > 4/n are reported; the model is refit without them as a sensitivity analysis. The trimmed refit is never the confirmatory result. (e) Model diagnostics and fallback. Gaussian models use the registered residual diagnostics; binary/ordinal generalized models use distribution-appropriate simulation or predictive diagnostics, not a Shapiro–Wilk residual gate. Appendix C must identify the exact estimator, tuning constants, inferential test and Bayesian evidence computation for each permitted fallback before lock. A fallback not so specified is a sensitivity analysis and cannot replace the primary confirmatory estimator.

methods_source_sections.heading: Bayesian prior sensitivity
methods_source_sections.text:
Sensitivity analyses

All confirmatory Bayesian conclusions are re-run under fixed prior transformations. Normal and HalfNormal priors: scale multiplied by 2 and by ½, location and support unchanged. Beta(2, 5) prior on η_RL: mean (2/7) preserved and concentration (sum of shape parameters, 7) multiplied by 2 and by ½, giving Beta(4, 10) and Beta(1, 2.5). Fixed parameters remain fixed or vary over a separately registered grid. Every evidence and interval criterion is recomputed under each sensitivity prior; if a conclusion crosses a §3.5.2 decision boundary (BF₁₀ = 3 or 100, BF₀₁ = 6), it is reported as prior-sensitive and reclassified as exploratory.

methods_source_sections.text:
